Issued at 306 AM EDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Today-Tonight...A weak upper trough extends down the Eastern 
Seaboard this morning, loosely influencing our weather pattern 
today, before being replaced by modest ridging mid week. Near normal 
temperatures are forecast, starting this morning with lows in the 
upper 60s to low 70s. Some mid and high level clouds are streaming 
northward, a sign of more upper level cloud cover to come through 
the day. Moisture will increase all day long, especially above 700mb 
and 400mb, with near-surface advection lagging behind. Weak 
southerly flow, at times a bit variable, will work against the 
development of the east coast sea breeze. We may still observe one, 
but it is likely to remain diffuse. 

Rain chances return today but very modestly. CAMs are not impressed 
with the convective environment today, partially due to delayed 
moisture advection during peak heating. With a lack of overall shear 
and instability among remnant dry air, 20-30% rain/storm chances are 
reasonable for the southern third of the area today. A shower or two 
can't be ruled out over far northern Lake/Volusia, either, in closer 
proximity to a stalled surface front over north FL/southern GA. 
Places that do see rain likely collect less than 0.10". Temperatures 
will reach the mid/upper 80s, despite additional mid/high clouds. 
With the added humidity later in the day, peak heat indices will 
push into the low 90s for most.

Dry conditions are forecast for a large portion of the area into 
early Wednesday, but a coastal shower or isolated storm cannot be 
ruled out as nocturnal activity develops near the Gulf Stream.

Wednesday-Thursday...A surface ridge axis is forecast to be centered 
over the Mid Atlantic region during this period. Weak H5 ridging 
also tries to build over central Florida as an upper level trough 
rotates through the Rockies and Central Plains. Moisture advection 
increases, especially Wednesday night into Thursday, as onshore flow 
speeds up a bit. Both days are likely to feature an inland-moving 
east coast breeze, perhaps a bit faster moving on Thursday, as 
breezy east winds peak around 20 mph at times. It is along the sea 
breeze in the afternoon where much of the rain and storm chances are 
focused, moving from east-to-west through mid evening. The highest 
rain chances Wednesday are anticipated along the Treasure Coast and 
near Lake Okeechobee, pushing toward Osceola/Orange/southern Lake 
counties into the evening. MLCAPE around 1000 J/kg and local forcing 
along the sea breeze will support shower and storm initiation, but 
weak lapse rates and a waterlogged column will likely limit stronger 
activity. Additional moisture arrives Thursday, allowing rain 
chances to spread farther north. Still, the better chances remain 
focused from Orlando/Melbourne southward, where greater daytime 
instability is forecast. Warming H5 temps will suppress an organized 
strong storm risk, but there could still be storms producing 
frequent lightning strikes, torrential downpours, and gusty winds. 
Afternoon temps are forecast to reach the upper 80s both days with 
overnight lows slightly above normal. 

Friday-Monday...Mid and upper level ridging is largely featured late 
week into the weekend as broad troughing affects the Upper Midwest, 
Great Lakes, and Northeast U.S. An unchanged onshore-flow pattern is 
forecast with deeper moisture overhead Friday, followed by modest 
mid/upper layer drying Sunday into Monday. This helps to tone down 
rain chances from 50-70% Friday to 30-50% this weekend and early 
next week. By early next week, a cold front is progged to reach 
north Florida and potentially slow or stall. Coincident with higher 
PW (2.0"+) across northern areas, this could help boost rain chances 
into the first full week of October. Temperatures look to remain 
slightly above normal through this extended period, ranging from the 
upper 80s/low 90s each day to the low/mid 70s overnight (warmer at 
the coast in onshore flow).
